quest_title: The Bridge That Hums at Night
fairytale_premise: Tomorrow morning, Mineral Springs Road in Porter, Indiana, reopens after almost three years. Tonight the new bridge is finished, floodlit and empty. The old steel beams lie stacked by the river, chewed hollow. Something under the water is humming, and it sounds hungry. Your flashlight finds fresh teeth marks on the brand-new rail.

the_threat.name: The Iron-Maw
the_threat.description: A long, shy river thing with rust-red teeth that licks and chews bridge steel until it flakes away. It hums when it feeds, and it has had three years to get hungry.
the_threat.mapped_from: Inspectors found the old bridge's steel beams had deteriorated; it closed Dec 1, 2023 as unsafe for all traffic.

the_goal.description: Drive the Iron-Maw back down the Little Calumet and keep the new span unchewed until the first car crosses at dawn.
the_goal.mapped_from: A newly built replacement bridge lets the road reopen after nearly three years.

locations.description: Orange barricades, a dark traffic light, and a span that hums when the wind is still.
locations.mapped_from: Road closed Dec 1 2023 as unsafe for traffic
locations.name: The Closed Bridge

locations.description: Muddy bank, shopping carts, and long scrape trails leading up to the steel beams.
locations.mapped_from: Bridge over Little Calumet River in Porter
locations.name: Little Calumet Riverbank

locations.description: Narrow county roads, tired detour signs, and a gas station with hand-drawn maps.
locations.mapped_from: Traffic detoured for nearly three years
locations.name: The Three-Year Detour

locations.description: Cranes, fresh concrete, new steel beams, and a night-shift trailer with floodlights.
locations.mapped_from: Replacement bridge built by contractor and inspected
locations.name: The New Span Work Site

complications.title: It Eats Your Tools
complications.what_happens: Flashlights flicker and anything iron left near the beams pits and flakes. The crowbar is gone. The team has to work with rope, wood and nerve.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Of course an iron-eater would snack on a crowbar too.
complications.mapped_from: Steel beams deteriorated and rusted through

complications.title: The Road Won't Stay Open
complications.what_happens: Detour signs spin and phones reroute everyone in circles. The team must map the loop on foot and mark the true path.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A closed road for three years forgets how to let people through.
complications.mapped_from: Road closed nearly three years with detour

complications.title: The Final Hum
complications.what_happens: The inspector's truck pulls up at dawn. The Iron-Maw picks that moment to hum, and the whole span shivers. Make it look like a bridge that passes.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: It always hummed loudest right before an inspection. That is how the old bridge failed one.
complications.mapped_from: New bridges are inspected before they reopen; the old one failed its inspection.

the_real_story.summary: A road in Porter, Indiana, closed for nearly three years is set to reopen with a newly built bridge.
the_real_story.headline: Road with new bridge in Porter to reopen after nearly 3 years
the_real_story.context_note: Likely Mineral Springs Road over the Little Calumet River, closed Dec 1, 2023 for deteriorated steel beams (Town of Porter notice). Verify against the article before demo.

art_style_hint: The floodlit new bridge on Mineral Springs Road at night, a rust-red river serpent coiled under the old stacked beams, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Billion Eggs That Crossed the Sea
realm_name: The North Sea coast, from the River Tyne to Mandø
fairytale_premise: A drone photographing the Danish island of Mandø finds the beach dotted with tiny white beads. Lab tests say they left an English river in July and crossed 390 miles of North Sea to get here, as if they knew the way. The gulls peck at them, then stop and stare at you. The beads are warm.

the_threat.description: A patient tide-thing that slipped a billion pale eggs into the Tyne in July and is herding them across the North Sea on the currents. They look exactly like fish roe.
the_threat.mapped_from: About one billion plastic nurdles (pre-production pellets) spilled into the River Tyne in July.
the_threat.name: The Hatch-Mother Tide

the_goal.description: Trace the eggs back to the Tyne, prove where they came from, and bag every last one before the Hatch-Mother calls them home.
the_goal.mapped_from: Denmark's EPA and Aarhus University linked the pellets to the Tyne spill; beach clean-up continues.

locations.description: Wide tidal flat where drone photos first showed white dots scattered on dark sand.
locations.mapped_from: Nurdles first spotted on Mandø 26 September
locations.name: Mandø White Strand

locations.description: Small garage office full of screens showing drone maps of the beach.
locations.mapped_from: Startup detected pellets using drone images
locations.name: The Drone Hut

locations.description: Bright university lab with microscopes and trays sorting pellets by size and color.
locations.mapped_from: Aarhus University tested pellets with EPA
locations.name: The Pellet Lab at Aarhus

locations.description: Windy German island beach where a second line of the same pellets was bagged.
locations.mapped_from: Samples also collected on Sylt, Germany
locations.name: Sylt South Beach

locations.description: A rusty riverside dock on the Tyne at low tide, where a billion pale beads went into the water in July. The mud still glitters.
locations.mapped_from: The July nurdle spill in the River Tyne, north-east England.
locations.name: Tyne Spill Dock

complications.title: The Gulls Won't Stop
complications.what_happens: Flocks land to eat the pale eggs and carry them inland, spreading the nest.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Hungry birds always think small round things are fish eggs.
complications.mapped_from: Birds mistake nurdles for fish eggs

complications.title: The Tide Brings More
complications.what_happens: Just as the beach looks clear, the high tide drops a fresh white line of eggs.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A billion eggs drifting 390 miles never arrive all at once.
complications.mapped_from: Arrival timing matched North Sea currents

complications.title: Everything Matches
complications.what_happens: The last lab test comes back: every bead has the same mother. That night, every bagged bead starts rolling toward the water at once.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: If no other spill fits, all eggs share one source.
complications.mapped_from: The agency found no other recorded spill that could explain the pellets: one source.

the_real_story.summary: Plastic pellets found on Denmark's coast likely came from a July spill of about one billion nurdles in England's River Tyne, about 390 miles away.
the_real_story.headline: Denmark nurdles may be from Tyne spill, agency says
the_real_story.context_note: Spill happened in July; pellets were first seen in Denmark on 26 September.

art_style_hint: Mandø's tidal flats at night glittering with pale beads under a drone spotlight, a vast shape moving under the waves, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

fairytale_premise: On the last day of the season at Polar Caves in Rumney, New Hampshire, the 80-ton boulder that hung over the walkway for a century finally lets go. Nobody is underneath. Nobody can say why. Tonight the park is locked, the stone is still warm, and if you press your ear to it, it is breathing very slowly.

the_threat.description: A cold grip left behind by the glacier that dropped these rocks. For a hundred years it held the boulder up over the walkway. On closing day it got tired and let go.
the_threat.mapped_from: The park has not given a cause for the 80-ton boulder's fall after more than a century.
the_threat.name: The Ice Age Grip

the_goal.description: Find out why the Grip let go, put it back to sleep, and keep the trail clear until the park reopens in 2027.
the_goal.mapped_from: The park will assess the site over the offseason and plans to reopen for the 2027 season.

locations.description: Narrow granite walls with a pale empty socket overhead where the rock hung for a century.
locations.mapped_from: Glacial talus caves left by continental glacier
locations.name: The Hollow Where It Hung

locations.description: Small hut with last-day tickets, lost hats, and a wall of visitor photos under the boulder.
locations.mapped_from: Fell Oct. 18 on final day, open since 1922
locations.name: Closing-Day Ticket Hut
The Talus Caves
locations.description: Tight crawlways between granite blocks the size of vans, dropped by a glacier. Cold air breathes out of the cracks even in October.
locations.mapped_from: Polar Caves are glacially formed talus caves from the last ice age.

locations.description: Cold trailer with trail maps, cones, and a 2027 reopening calendar on the wall.
locations.mapped_from: Park to assess site in offseason
locations.name: Winter Watch Trailer

locations.description: Splintered boards pinned under 80 tons of stone, blocking any walk past.
locations.mapped_from: Wooden walkway used by thousands, now smashed
locations.name: The Smashed Boardwalk

complications.title: The Trail Is Blocked
complications.what_happens: The boulder seals the narrow passage. Loose rocks tick down. You must rig a rope line and spot each other to get around safely.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: An 80-ton rock does not land neatly. Of course the only way through is blocked.
complications.mapped_from: 80-ton rock smashed walkway and blocks trail

complications.title: The Gates Are Locking
complications.what_happens: Staff close the gates for winter. Lights go out. Your phones lose signal, and you must work by flashlight and shouted directions.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: It fell on closing day. Of course there is nobody left to keep the power on.
complications.mapped_from: Fell on final day of season, park now closed

complications.title: It Shifts Again
complications.what_happens: The stone groans and settles deeper. You must freeze, listen together, then coax it still with steady weight and wedged boards.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Freshly fallen rock keeps moving. Of course it was not done settling on night one.
complications.mapped_from: No cause given, site to be assessed

the_real_story.summary: Polar Caves in Rumney says its 80-ton hanging boulder fell on Oct. 18, smashing a walkway, with no injuries reported.
the_real_story.headline: Massive 80-ton boulder comes crashing down after more than a century at New Hampshire attraction
the_real_story.context_note: Nobody was hurt; the park has not said what caused the fall.

art_style_hint: A granite cave trail in the New Hampshire woods at night, an 80-ton boulder on a smashed boardwalk with pale frost-hands still cupping it, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Signal That Wakes Up Hungry
realm_name: The Very Large Array, New Mexico
fairytale_premise: At 2 a.m., every dish at the Very Large Array in the New Mexico desert swings toward the same empty patch of sky. The printout shows a radio source that was not there in 1996. It flared in 2014, went quiet, then woke up again last winter. Tonight its pitch keeps changing while you listen, like it is trying to find your frequency.

the_threat.description: A dark, hungry mouth circling a bright companion star, sipping its light and singing radio songs across decades. Every time it feeds, it gets louder.
the_threat.mapped_from: The leading explanation is an accreting black hole or neutron star pulling material from a companion star.
the_threat.name: The Far Feeder

the_goal.description: Pin down the signal's source and prove it is a hungry thing 49,000 light-years away feeding on a star, not something knocking on Earth's door.
the_goal.mapped_from: Astronomers' leading idea: a black hole or neutron star feeding on a companion star, far beyond the Norma-Cygnus arm.

locations.description: A low-lit control room full of monitors, printouts, and cold coffee where the sky survey scrolls past.
locations.mapped_from: Very Large Array Sky Survey data in New Mexico
locations.name: Night-Shift Control Room

locations.description: Dusty shelves of old sky maps and hard drives, with a blank page where the signal should be.
locations.mapped_from: Absent in 1996 survey, bright by 2014
locations.name: Archive Trailer

locations.description: A small concrete shed with headphones and dials for catching the shifting radio pitch.
locations.mapped_from: Spectrum peak jumping and no X-rays found
locations.name: Listening Shed

locations.description: Rows of huge white dishes pointed at black sky, humming faintly as they track the same spot.
locations.mapped_from: VLA radio telescope array in New Mexico
locations.name: The Dish Field

complications.title: The Missing First Tape
complications.what_happens: The old 1996 survey shows empty sky where the signal should be, so your charts will not line up.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: You cannot track something that was asleep before you started looking.

complications.title: The Station Keeps Moving
complications.what_happens: Every tuned receiver goes quiet because the signal jumps to a new radio pitch while you listen.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A restless singer will not stay on one note for long.

complications.title: It Wakes Up Again
complications.what_happens: Just as you finish logging it, the monitors spike bright again for one final flare.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A thing that flares every few years was always due for one more show.

the_real_story.summary: Astronomers found a distant radio source, VT J1906+0849, that appeared, faded and brightened again over decades in ways that match no known type of object.
the_real_story.headline: A Strange Radio Signal in The Far Reaches of The Milky Way Is Behaving Like Nothing Else in The Galaxy
the_real_story.context_note: No danger to Earth; source is at least 49,000 light-years away.

art_style_hint: The white dishes of the Very Large Array in the New Mexico desert at night, all aimed at one point where an impossible beam of light falls from deep space, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Pumpkin That Hums at Nap Time
fairytale_premise: At the Fall Fun Festival in Hysham, Montana, the weigh-off winner is a 280-pound pumpkin grown by a two-year-old. After dark it sits by the hay bales under string lights. The vines are still growing, an inch every time you look away. The scale reads 280 with nothing on it. The kid just says it hums at nap time.

the_threat.description: An old root-mind under the patch that hears lullabies and puffs pumpkins huge overnight.
the_threat.mapped_from: A 280-pound pumpkin, grown locally by a 2-year-old, won the festival weigh-off.
the_threat.name: The Patch That Listens

the_goal.description: Get the humming champion onto the festival scale for an honest weigh-in, and lull the patch back to sleep before the vines take the fairground.
the_goal.mapped_from: The 280-pound pumpkin won the Fall Fun Festival weigh-off.

locations.description: A fenced backyard patch with trampled vines, one huge hollow pumpkin, and a tiny watering can.
locations.mapped_from: locally grown giant pumpkin
locations.name: The Toddler's Pumpkin Patch

locations.description: Food tables, game booths, and flyers for the Fall Fun Festival in small-town Hysham.
locations.mapped_from: Fall Fun Festival in Hysham Montana
locations.name: Festival Midway Row

locations.description: A heavy steel platform scale beside the festival tent, its old dial needle trembling and its bulbs flickering with nothing on it.
locations.mapped_from: festival weigh-in scale
locations.name: The Weigh-Off Scale

locations.description: A stubble field with hay bales, string lights, and a tractor waiting for evening hayrides.
locations.mapped_from: typical fall-festival hayrides and fields
locations.name: Hayride Field at Dusk

complications.title: It Will Not Roll
complications.what_happens: The 280-pound pumpkin sinks, sticks, and leans away from the truck every time you push.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Of course a thing that grew that fast holds the dirt tight.
complications.mapped_from: Moving giant pumpkins is notoriously tricky

complications.title: The Scale Is Awake
complications.what_happens: The festival scale buzzes and reads heavy with nothing on it, lights flickering in rhythm.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Of course the scale noticed all that extra growing energy first.
complications.mapped_from: Festival weigh-in scale and weigh-off contest

complications.title: Nap-Time Price
complications.what_happens: The vines wrap the festival gate and will not let go. They only loosen for the nap-time song, and nobody on the team knows the words.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Of course it only listens to the voice that sang to it all summer.

the_real_story.summary: A 280-pound locally grown pumpkin won the weigh-off at the Fall Fun Festival in Hysham, Montana.
the_real_story.headline: A 2-year-old grew the 280-pound winning pumpkin at Hysham's Fall Fun Festival
the_real_story.context_note: The young grower is unnamed in coverage; keep it that way in play.

art_style_hint: A small-town Montana fall festival at night, one enormous glowing pumpkin by the hay bales with vines creeping over the fairground, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.
